explanations.explanation: Oh, friend, I wish it were that easy. The LORD opens with the opposite: "The LORD was very angry with your fathers." (Zechariah 1:2) That's how the message to Zechariah, the prophet, begins. Pleased and very angry are not the same thing.

Right, and the LORD doesn't ease into it. He says, "The LORD was very angry with your fathers." (Zechariah 1:2) That's the first thing Zechariah, the prophet, hears in this message. No warm-up, no small talk, just the plain truth up front.

explanations.answer: They return to Him and He returns to them
explanations.explanation: Yes, and listen to how it's built. "Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you…" (Zechariah 1:3) The people take the first step, and the LORD promises to meet them. I think that's about the warmest door anybody ever held open.

explanations.answer: They bring offerings and He forgives them
explanations.explanation: I see why that sounds right, since offerings are all over the Bible. But this message doesn't mention them. The LORD says, "Return to Me… and I will return to you…" (Zechariah 1:3) It's about the people coming back to Him, and Him coming back to them.

explanations.answer: They rebuild His house and He blesses them
explanations.explanation: That one's got a nice ring to it, but it's not what the LORD says here. In this message He says, "Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you…" (Zechariah 1:3) The call is to come back to Him, and the promise is that He comes back to them. Simple as that.

That's it. The LORD says of the fathers, "…they did not listen or pay attention to Me…" (Zechariah 1:4) The former prophets were the earlier messengers He sent them. The message was clear, and the fathers kept on walking. Listening is free, friend, and they still skipped it.

If only! That would've made for a short story. The LORD says the opposite: "…they did not listen or pay attention to Me…" (Zechariah 1:4) The former prophets, the earlier messengers He sent, said to turn, and the fathers didn't.

Good guess, but the text doesn't say that. It says, "…they did not listen or pay attention to Me…" (Zechariah 1:4) The earlier messengers told them to turn from their evil ways and deeds. No sign requested, just no listening.

Yes! God asks, "But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers?" (Zechariah 1:6) The prophets carried the message, but the words came from Him. And those words caught up. I once hid in a drawer for years, and let me tell you, running from a thing doesn't work.

A famine is a fair thing to guess, since the Bible has plenty of them. But that's not what God names here. He asks, "But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers?" (Zechariah 1:6) It's His words that did the overtaking.

Big weather, big drama, I get it. But God doesn't name a storm. He asks, "But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers?" (Zechariah 1:6) His words and statutes are what caught up with them.

True! After His words overtook them, the fathers "repented and said…" (Zechariah 1:6) That means they finally turned around. The message they brushed off earlier caught up with them, and they came to see it.

Not quite, and here's the good part. The text says, "They repented and said…" (Zechariah 1:6) So the fathers did repent once His words caught up with them. The story of those fathers has a turn in it.

Yes! The fathers said, "Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us." (Zechariah 1:6) They looked back and saw that what happened matched what He said He would do. That's a humble thing to say out loud, friend.

Close in sound, far in meaning. Nobody says the LORD refused anything here. The fathers said, "Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us." (Zechariah 1:6) He did what He purposed.

That's a thoughtful guess, like a cookie sitting by the oven door deciding. But the fathers don't say He hesitated. They said, "Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us." (Zechariah 1:6) What He purposed is what He did.
